en.headline: HK Electric opens smart operations centre to speed emergency repairs
en.dek: The centre, launched in June ahead of typhoon season, integrates AI, IoT sensors and live video links so engineers can locate cable faults and coordinate repairs more quickly.
body: Hongkong Electric has opened an Intelligent Operations and Emergency Response Centre to improve the resilience of its power grid during extreme weather and other incidents. The facility began operations in June before the main typhoon season.

The centre consolidates data from more than ten internal monitoring platforms onto a single visual interface. About 1,500 sensors and smart devices across Hong Kong Island and Lamma Power Station feed real-time information through the company’s self-developed SmartLink network.

Key tools include a low-voltage fault indicator system that can narrow the location of a cable fault to within about one kilometre, reducing the time needed to inspect, repair and restore supply from roughly two hours to 40–50 minutes. AI analysis of temperature, humidity and flood data helps prioritise work at multiple substations.

A live-video system known as LENS allows frontline staff wearing smart helmets or carrying portable cameras to stream images and audio back to the centre. Support staff can then project engineering drawings onto the helmets and maintain continuous communication while monitoring safety conditions.

zh.headline: 港燈啟用智能營運及緊急應變中心 加快搶修
zh.dek: 中心於6月風季前投入服務，結合人工智能、物聯網感應器及即時視像，協助迅速定位電纜故障及協調前線搶修。
body: 香港電燈有限公司啟用智能營運及緊急應變中心，提升極端天氣及突發事故下的電網應變能力。中心於今年6月颱風季節前開始運作。
中心將超過十個內部監察平台的資訊整合於同一可視化介面，並透過公司自主研發的「智連網」，接收分布港島各區及南丫發電廠約1,500個感應器及智能設備的實時數據。
當中包括全球首創的低壓故障指示器系統，可將懷疑故障電纜範圍縮至約一公里內，把以往約兩小時的檢查、維修及復電時間縮短至40至50分鐘。人工智能亦可分析溫度、濕度及水浸數據，協助安排多個變電站的搶修優次。
名為LENS的即時視像系統則讓前線人員透過智能頭盔或隨身攝錄機，將現場畫面及語音傳回中心。後方人員可將工程圖紙投射至頭盔螢幕，並持續通訊及監察安全狀況。
